domain: multi-agent autonomous software engineering studio / orchestration control plane
objective: End-to-end multi-agent software engineering studio and orchestration engine that exceeds Paseo, iPolloWork, and Orkas across four pillars: hierarchical manager-worker coordination with task DAGs; deterministic git worktree isolation & concurrent merge reconciliation; dynamic least-privilege MCP/tool scoping against context flooding; high-density operator cockpit design language.
entities: Manager / Tech Lead agent (human-facing scope negotiator, epic -> DAG decomposer)
Researcher / Explorer agent (indexing, dependency analysis, doc synthesis)
Implementer / Coder agent (isolated feature + bugfix delivery)
Auditor / Reviewer agent (static analysis, lint, test regression, security/diff gate)
Task DAG node (epic -> story -> task, typed artifacts, evidence receipts)
Git worktree + ephemeral branch (unit of coder isolation)
Staging / integration branch + merge queue (reconciliation point)
Tool Manifest / Role Capability Set (least-privilege tool slice per agent)
MCP Router / Tool Proxy Gateway (dynamic schema slicing)
Session Bridge / Harness Adapter (Claude Code, OpenCode, pi, headless loops)
Event Log / Execution Trace / Token Ledger
Operator Cockpit (War Room, Agent Stream, Audit Gate, MCP Registry)
constraints: No working-tree collisions between concurrent coder agents
Tool schema count per agent session must stay bounded (anti-context-flooding: 50+ tool schemas exhaust context and raise hallucination rate)
Deterministic worktree lifecycle: create, sync, teardown must be idempotent and crash-safe (no disk leaks)
Every merge into staging must pass an automated auditor gate before landing
Token accounting must be attributable per sub-agent, per task, per turn
Manager agent <-> human negotiation must be resumable and auditable
Must wrap heterogeneous CLI harnesses without forking them (stdio/PTY/JSON-RPC/ACP)
Coordination overhead must not itself dominate token budget (see: zero-token coordination, bernstein)
Teardown of orphaned worktrees/branches after crash or timeout is mandatory
This phase is research/architecture/design ONLY - no application code generation

All five implement real lifecycle; none is merely advisory.

notable_patterns_observed_in_ecosystem: Vigil: manager runs the tree, workers + sub-managers, detail down / summaries up
YYLO: typed task + validation + merge + release-readiness boundaries, risk-based merge queue, receipt-backed changes
foremerge: agents DECLARE INTENT + semantic scope BEFORE writing; deterministic collision rules
wit: function-level (Tree-sitter) locks rather than file locks, warns before write
Zaivern Code: line-level ownership to prevent merge conflicts
gastown: Bors-style merge queue + health watchdogs at 20-30 agent scale
OrcaReplay: record at process+socket boundary so model traffic, exit codes, file deltas and MCP JSON-RPC share one timeline; offline replay + fork-at-checkpoint
bernstein: zero-token coordination (no model in the coordination loop), verify with tests
Tempest: shared local code-knowledge graph cuts token use across sessions
Fletch: each agent in own clone under Seatbelt/Docker, shared symbol+call-graph index served over MCP
neuralyzer: agent wipes its own session context and re-runs (Ralph-loop engineering)
aGiTrack: each turn committed to git with prompt/model/token-cost in the commit message
Concord MCP: claim work, detect edit collisions, transfer ownership, hand off review evidence
paperclip: agents wake on heartbeats to claim tickets under org charts, budgets, approval gates
no_human: second model in fresh session told to REFUTE 'done'; tamper guard blocks net test reductions
loki-mode: 41 agents / 8 swarms / nine quality gates / blind three-reviewer review
